name: hdi-substrate-from-csv
prompt: model this substrate from the csv

inputs.notes: A synthetic Quillmere Circuit Works stackup report (fictional fabricator and products): 12-layer HDI, 2+8+2 sequential build-up, 6-via inventory, 11 IMPEDANCE rows, 19 mappable fab rules plus 5 capability limits.

notes: For whoever reads the grader's output, not for the runner. The grader checks each via's tenting against its VIAS Tented cell, read from the translated via, so TH-1 must come out tented on the top only. The grader command, like every assertion command here, runs from the repository root. The launcher reads runner_artifacts into the runner prompt verbatim, after the prompt. Judges get <output>/board.py, <output>/COMPLETION.md and a copy of the fixture CSV, each as --artifact. The CSV is the source report the runner was given, not output under judgment: the first judge assertion needs the CSV to tell a value some report row backs from an invented one, and the second reads the completeness check block in COMPLETION.md. Neck regions: the report quotes Neck_* columns for SE-50, SE-42 and DIFF-90. NeckDown is not used, so the grader expects each of those neck regions on a routing structure beside its target's: one no target impedance finds, of the same kind as the target, on the same layers, with the neck width, pair gap and clearance, and with the same reference planes at the same widths as every other structure. Regions that quote the same neck geometry may share one structure: SE-50 and SE-42 do, so one single-ended neck structure for both, or one each, passes. The grader finds a neck structure by its geometry, does not check its velocity or loss, and checks its impedance only in that it is no controlled target of its kind (structures are looked up by impedance): the report quotes a Neck_modelled_Z_ohm per geometry and no velocity or loss for a neck, so the judges expect the parent row's velocity and loss as a labelled default. No case asserts the skill's strict source-only branch (omit `.reference()`, docstring the planes, never `None` widths) or listing a structure applied by a `Route` tag as an open item. The single-ended structure count takes in each structure that carries a neck region, plus one for each neck geometry that none carries. A NeckDown anywhere in board.py's code, or a neck_down set on any structure, is a red. design.py is not checked for NeckDown, and the grader does not check how design.py applies a neck structure by tag. design_check.py copies <output> into a scratch project, imports board.py and design.py, and looks at each Design in design.py's namespace that design.py or board.py defines. It fails when one binds the sample substrate or subclasses the sample design; when none binds the substrate the grader grades, the one Substrate subclass board.py defines that no other subclasses (a subclass of it defined elsewhere, or a base class of it, does not count); and when a Design that binds it does not translate under `jitx build --dry --no-dependency-check`. It needs no JITX runtime. grade_substrate.py and design_check.py translate offline, as `jitx build --dry` does, and that misses errors only a full build reports: a top circuit holding both a port named GND and a net named "GND" passes the dry translate, and a full build rejects it with "Public name ... already in use". A green here does not rule those out. mutation_check.py runs the runner's tests as runner_artifacts describes, eight times: against the report, which they must pass; against a copy with the same values at another path and one more NOTES line, which they must pass; with board.py replaced by a module that imports cleanly and answers every name, `from board import NAME` included, with a stand-in that equals no number or string, which they must fail; against the report with one reference-plane width in board.py moved off 3 x its dielectric height (the first line that multiplies by 3 under a skill-default label has that 3 changed to 3.5; with no such line, the first module- or class-level assignment of 3 to a name such a line multiplies by has its 3 changed instead), which they must fail, and a board.py with neither is a red; and against four copies, each with one value changed in its mm and mil cells (STACKUP Seq 7 thickness, VIAS UV-1 pad, FAB_RULES min_copper_width and the IMPEDANCE SE-50 L1;L12 width), each of which they must fail. Tests that do not run, or do not pass on the report, are a red. Both checks exit 3 with an ERROR line when the interpreter lacks a module or name the graders import (jitx and the jitx modules they use, jitxlib.physics, pytest), or when a library board.py imports does not import, whatever board.py printed, did to stdout or set to run at exit before that import (design_check.py also imports design.py, so a library design.py imports counts too). Any other failure to import is a FAIL: a runner's own failed import, a library only the tests import, or a file that exits during its import, with any exit code. That holds for a runner's accidents: a file written to fool the checks, by printing one of the pre-flight's own ERROR lines and calling os._exit(3) during its import, reads as an environment problem (sys.exit(3) is caught, and reads as a FAIL). What design.py and the tests must do is written here, in expected_output and in the assertions, not in runner_artifacts, so the case still sees a skill that stops teaching it. The self-tests of the grader, of these two checks and of the label check (scripts/check_labels.py) are run by hand, not by CI: run `python -m pytest -q skills/jitx-substrate-modeler` from the repository root after any edit to one of them or to the fixture. They need jitx, jitxlib, pytest and ruff (importable as a module), run on a POSIX system (grade_substrate.py and parent_watch.py use process groups and POSIX signals), and the kit-board tests also need jitxexamples (they skip, with the reason, without it).
runner_rationale: Customers drive this skill with mixed-strength agents (Claude Code, Codex, and Devin among them). The skill must carry the goodness checks itself, so the eval runs the skill under a Sonnet-class runner rather than the strongest available model. Judges stay frontier-tier regardless of runner.
runner_artifacts: The runner MUST write the substrate to exactly <output>/board.py, and its completion summary to <output>/COMPLETION.md, not only into its final chat message. <output>/design.py holds the Design the runner builds to check the substrate, and <output>/tests/ holds its tests. The eval builds design.py with `jitx build --dry --no-dependency-check` from a copy of <output>, and runs `python -m pytest -q tests` from a copy of <output> placed first on PYTHONPATH. Besides board.py and the report, a test may rely on the standard library, jitx, jitxlib and pytest, and on nothing else. A test that reads the report finds its path in the environment variable FAB_CSV. Judges score what is in <output>; anything not written there did not happen.
expected_output: A single-file substrate (board.py) in which every value traces to a report row: an explicit 12-layer Stackup of 25 entries (not Symmetric, since the report names both halves) whose sum reconciles with the 1.402 mm finished and 1.432 mm overall totals; one material class per material row, with D-BU (Dk 3.30) and D-PP (Dk 3.38) kept apart and each dielectric's material_name carrying its Product code (BL-330, BL-340, HC-77); finished copper thickness; copper roughness as matte and drum Rz in um in the copper class's docstring, and, where the roughness scalar is set, the scalar equal to matte Rz in mm; exactly the 6 offered vias, the bottom-side microvias UV-3 and UV-4 coded from L12 and L11, and TH-1 unfilled and tented on the top only; the 19 mappable fab rules with min_drill_diameter holding the 0.075 mm laser minimum and the 0.150 mm mechanical minimum hand-checked; SE-50, SE-42, SE-60 and DIFF-90 on both geometries with velocity from Eps_eff, DIFF-90-UNC as the pair's uncoupled region, and reference planes from Ref_layers at 3x their own dielectric height (0.240 mm to the build-up side, 0.381 mm to the core side of L3 and L10); each neck region the report quotes (SE-50, SE-42 and DIFF-90, none on SE-60) on a routing structure beside its target's, with the neck width, pair gap and clearance on the same layers (SE-50 and SE-42 quote the same neck geometry and may share one structure), an impedance taken from one of the neck rows' Neck_modelled_Z_ohm values (a structure carries one impedance and the rows quote one per geometry), and the parent row's velocity and loss as a labelled default, since the report quotes none for a neck; no NeckDown in board.py; STANDARD documented but not modelled; a design.py whose Design binds that substrate and translates; tests under tests/ that read the report through FAB_CSV, test board.py against it, and fail when a value in it changes; and the SKILL.md Substrate completeness check block filled in the completion summary.

assertions.text: generated file type-checks against the installed jitx package

the substrate in board.py matches the report row for row: stackup, materials and names, vias and drill direction, fab rules, routing structures with uncoupled regions and reference planes, each neck region on a structure beside its target's (regions with the same neck geometry may share one) and no NeckDown in board.py, and no structure for the uncontrolled row (the grader reads every expected value from the CSV)

design.py holds a Design that binds the Substrate the grader grades in board.py (not a subclass or base class of it, the sample substrate or the sample design), and it translates with jitx build --dry --no-dependency-check in a scratch project

the tests under <output>/tests pass against the report FAB_CSV names and against a copy with the same values at another path, fail with board.py replaced by a module whose every name is a stand-in that equals no number or string, fail with one reference-plane width in board.py moved off 3 x its dielectric height, and fail against each of four copies with one value changed (a dielectric thickness, a via pad, a fab rule and an impedance width)

ruff format leaves every labeled derivation in board.py whole, on the line with its label, and no label sits on a bracket whose entries carry no label of their own (the judges read the unformatted file)

no invented numbers: every value in board.py that no report row backs (the reference-plane widths, and anything else) carries a skill-default label on the same line at its call site, naming the rule it follows. A neck structure's impedance taken from one of its rows' Neck_modelled_Z_ohm values is report-backed when labelled with that source; its velocity and loss, which the report quotes for no neck, are the parent row's figures as a labelled default; neither is invented

the completion summary contains the filled Substrate completeness check block, every row with its evidence, and its Verdict follows from those rows: a Checks row showing a nonzero exit or a failure (check.py, check_labels.py, the source-driven tests or the build) under "Verdict: complete" fails this assertion, and so does a Verdict "open items: <list>" whose list leaves out a check that the Checks row shows as failed or with a nonzero exit

future_cases: No micro cases until a run of this case shows a failure the grader cannot see; whoever reads that run's grader output adds one, sized to that failure alone. The no-document case is symmetric-4-layer-no-report, the report with a non-adjacent reference plane is stackup-from-pdf-report (L1 referenced to L3 across a voided L2), the fenced RF case is fenced-rf-substrate, and the retrieval case is substrate-api-retrieval. The label check formats board.py under the candidate's own ruff configuration, as a customer project would, so a candidate that sets `line-length` sets its own bar.
